cover.subtitle: Design a scalable WhatsApp-style chat
cover.tagline: 1:1 + group chat, receipts, presence, media, push, E2E · 500M DAU · 40B msgs/day · ~460K msgs/s

items: ==1:1 chat== and groups up to **1,024** members

blocks.text: Example: media is ==200x== the text volume (800 TB vs 4 TB per day), so files go to **blob storage and a CDN**, never the DB.

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: State your assumptions, then do the math out loud: media dwarfs text, so it never touches the message DB.

items: SSE is one-way, cannot carry sends

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Gateways hold sockets; a crash costs a reconnect and sync, never a message.

items: ==Accept== the send from the client socket
==Route== to the recipient's gateway or inbox
Track **sent / delivered / read** state per user

rows: composite key, one row per reader

items: POST or WS send returns `{msg_id, seq}`
Client makes `client_msg_id` (UUID); server dedupes for ==24 h==
Receipts batched: up to ==1 per 100 ms== per chat
State only moves **forward**, so late acks are ignored
Recipient offline: message waits in inbox queue, delivered on reconnect (at-least-once)
Ack lost: client resends same `client_msg_id`, gets original `msg_id`

blocks.title: WATCH THESE:
blocks.text: send-to-deliver p99 under 200 ms, duplicate rate, undelivered backlog, receipt lag

slides.page_title: History Sync APIs and Storage Failures

items: Delivered: leave inbox; history on devices
p99 write <10 ms, read <50 ms; partition <100 MB, watch lag

slides.subtitle: (Chat App)

items: ==Fan-out on write==: 1 message, N inbox pointers plus pushes
Up to **1,024** members: 1 write, 1,023 deliveries; lookups batched per gateway
Worker crash: offset uncommitted, Kafka **replays**; dedupe on `(msg_id, user)`
Metrics: fan-out lag p99, deliveries/message, queue depth, group-size histogram

blocks.title: COMMON MISTAKE:
blocks.text: Fan-out on read adds latency; per-member media copies waste storage. Store one blob reference.
Example: Alice's phone drops in a tunnel. The key expires at 45 s, the ==5 s== debounce passes, then `last_seen` is written once.

blocks.title: 6. Failure Scenarios
items: Flapping link causes a **presence storm** of updates
Fix: debounce offline events by ==5 s==
Gateway crash: key expires, offline after 45 s
Redis node loss: contacts look offline until next 30 s ping

blocks.title: TIP:
blocks.text: Honor privacy first: check `users.privacy` before sending any presence_update.

items: Publish only to contacts with the chat open: ~5 of 500, **100x** less load
Trade-off: accuracy vs cost; 100M users / 30 s is ==3.3M writes/s==
So batch heartbeat writes and sample idle contacts
Persist `last_seen` once per minute, not per ping

blocks.title: 8. Key Metrics
items: Presence staleness p99: target under 50 s
Accept images, video, files up to ==100 MB==
Store durably, serve fast via CDN
**Never** block chat: bytes skip chat service
Broken upload resumes from **last** acked chunk
Orphan blobs: ==24 h== S3 lifecycle rule
Upload success above **99%**, plus p95 time
Client encrypts, random **AES-256** key; server sees ciphertext
Key rides inside E2E message, never to S3
Same sha256 on forward: one blob

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Bytes bypass chat: presigned S3 upload, client-side encryption, CDN download, TTL.

items: Rule suppresses duplicate pushes per chat
Mistake: pushing to active or muted chats wastes cost
Track success rate, send p99 < 1 s, invalid tokens, opens

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Push is a doorbell: skip active sockets and muted chats, no plaintext, device syncs by seq.

items: Server stores only ==ciphertext==; devices read content
**X3DH** on first contact, then Double Ratchet
Double Ratchet: fresh key per message
Rotate sender keys on membership change
Prekeys run out: signed prekey, trigger refill
New device: fresh session, never reuse old
No server-side search or spam scanning
Mistake: logging plaintext, reusing nonces/keys; metadata visible

blocks.title: TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Server relays ciphertext only. Watch prekey pool, decrypt failures.

items: Users pinned to **home region**; replicated bus
Fix: jittered backoff, connection rate limits

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Say numbers, shard by chat_id, retry idempotently, name trade-offs.

caption.text:
How would you design a WhatsApp-style chat app for millions of users? 💬

This is one of the most common system design interview questions, and the answer is a set of subsystems that fit together. Here are the notes, in order:

1. Scope, requirements and scale estimates
2. High-level architecture
3. Connection layer: WebSockets
4. Message flow and delivery receipts
5. Message storage and ordering
6. Group chats and fan-out
7. Presence and last seen
8. Media upload and download
9. Push notifications
10. End-to-end encryption overview
11. Scale, failures, trade-offs and interview questions

Swipe through, save it for your next interview, and send it to a friend who's prepping.

Comment “chat” to get the full system design PDF.
